the silver nanoparticles tested in this study had a significant effect on the growth of all microorganisms tested.

the silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) used here have a strong effect on the growth dynamics of Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis), and that the effect of the AgNPs on the growth dynamics depends on their surface charge.
silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have a significant effect on the growth of Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

the effects of silver nanoparticles on the growth dynamics of microorganisms.

the effects of silver nanoparticles on growth dynamics of micro‐organisms, including Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and the effects of the nanoparticles on the growth dynamics of the micro‐organisms are evaluated by the cultivation‐based assay.

the silver nanoparticles are toxic for all the tested bacteria.

the effects of silver nanoparticles are highly dependent on the test system used.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of conventional growth‐inhibition assays may not be sufficient to fully characterize the effects of silver nanoparticles on micro‐organism growth, as the effects may be time‐dependent.

the dynamic growth profiles of bacteria and fungi can be used to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of silver nanoparticles in a time‐resolved manner, and that the dynamic growth curves are sensitive enough to detect the differences in antimicrobial effects of different silver nanoparticles.
a cultivation‐based approach can be used for time‐resolved susceptibility testing of nanoparticles and that this method is suitable for high‐throughput screening.
